name: NVIDIA L40S
memory_bandwidth_basis: GDDR6 18Gbps x 384-bit = 864 GB/s. Bus width is the standard AD102 384-bit; NVIDIA's L40 datasheet prints only the 864 GB/s aggregate.
notes: AUDIT CORRECTION: the dense/sparse flag on the tensor rows was inverted. FP16 362 / FP8 733 TFLOPS are DENSE. NVIDIA L40S page prints FP16 '362.05 | 733*' and FP8 '733 | 1,466*' where *=With Sparsity; the dense value is the LEFT column. These rows were previously flagged dense:false, which wrongly told a reader they were sparse.  The stored numbers are correct dense values. CRITICAL: NVIDIA prints dense|sparse pairs explicitly on the L40 sheet, e.g. FP16 '362.05 | 733*' and FP8 '733 | 1,466*'. The DENSE values are recorded here (362 / 733) and marked dense:true; the sparse values are 733 / 1,466. This is the clearest example of the sparsity trap in the whole lineup - the marketing headline for L40S is 733 'FP8 TFLOPS' and that is already the DENSE number, while other vendors' 733 figures are sparse. FP32 91.6 and RT Core 212 are dense. NOTE the source is the L40 datasheet rather than an L40S-specific one: it marks its numbers 'preliminary, subject to change'. L40S and L40 both print 48GB / 864 GB/s but differ in power (350W vs 300W) and in CUDA count; treat the L40 sheet as L40S-family, not L40-exact. No NVLink, no MIG - GDDR6 cannot be partitioned. No 'other' row: Ada has no FP64 hardware path.
